svg.title: Invariant densities and extremal transverse measures
svg.desc: A proof diagram with exact inverse modulus, weighted fibre mean and variance, saturated good fibres, and ergodic constant density. It applies under sigma-finite unit measure, obtained on a conull support from nonzero semifinite ergodicity.

g.text: Ergodicity makes a transverse density constant
Measurable groupoid · faithful proper ν · fixed positive finite modulus δ
Obtain sigma-finiteness before using a density
Nonzero semifinite + ergodic Λ ⇒ saturated conull B with finite faithful ρ
On B, μ = Λν is σ-finite. Dominated Θ ≤ Λ gives Θν = f μ, 0 ≤ f ≤ 1.
Modular symmetry on the arrow measure m = μ ∘ ν
m̃ = δ⁻¹m and m̃₁ = δ⁻¹m₁ ⇒ f ∘ s = f ∘ r almost everywhere for m
A positive properness weight detects essential constancy
a(x) = νˣ(w (f ∘ s))/q(x); v(x) = νˣ(w (f ∘ s − a(x))²)/q(x)
C = {v = 0} is saturated. F = 1C a is strictly invariant and equals f μ-a.e.
Ergodicity and faithful-function determination finish the proof
Every rational level set of F is null or conull ⇒ F = c almost everywhere
Θ = cΛ. Conversely, two nonnegligible invariant parts give a nonproportional split.
The weight w need not be invariant; its positivity preserves the fibre null sets.
Proof: Lemmas 2.1–2.2, Corollary 2.3, Theorem 3.1. Connes: author-hosted PDF 44, Corollary 8.
